Keys: 4c4a:4a55:port=PCIROOT(0)#PCI(1400)#USBROOT(0)/13.1.3 | 1532:0e05:port=PCIROOT(0)#PCI(1C04)#PCI(0000)#PCI(0200)#PCI(0000)#USBROOT(0)/4.4 | 046d:085c:sn=B76395EF | 046d:0843:port=PCIROOT(0)#PCI(1400)#USBROOT(0)/13.1.4 (scratchpad verify_naming/time_camera_identity.json).

verdicts.claim: Windows ignores a USB serial containing chars <= 0x20, > 0x7F or ','; udev usb_id applies almost the same rule (< 0x20, > 0x7f, ',') citing the same MS guidance; camera_identity applies the stricter Windows rule.
verdicts.reason: The udev part is confirmed in the downloaded v255 udev-builtin-usb_id.c (lines 403-419): '*p < 0x20 || *p > 0x7f || *p == ','' with a comment citing msdn gg487321. camera_identity.py line 54 implements 0x20 < c <= 0x7F and c != ','. The Windows part is overstated. The cited MS blog says these characters 'are not allowed' and warns of a possible bugcheck. It does NOT say Windows ignores or falls back from such a serial. What Windows actually does with an invalid serial is untested and undocumented in the cited source.
verdicts.rerun_numbers: Source read only (documented-untested).

verdicts.claim: On Linux, 60-persistent-v4l.rules gives /dev/v4l/by-id/usb-$ID_SERIAL-video-index$N (ID_SERIAL = vendor_model[_serial], so serial-less identical cameras collide) and /dev/v4l/by-path/$ID_PATH-video-index$N, where path_id replaces the USB host number with 0; an app can resolve a stable key without root.
verdicts.reason: The source claims are accurate. 60-persistent-v4l.rules main and v255 both have sha256 d5a6c72c..., and the by-id rule is $env{ID_BUS}-$env{ID_SERIAL}-video-index$attr{index}. usb_id builds vendor_model[_serial]. path_id.c line 554 says to drop the host number and always use '0', and also prepends 'usbv<rev>-0:' (ID_PATH_WITH_USB_REVISION) to avoid USB2/USB3 root-hub collisions. Behaviour on real Linux hardware is untested. The WSL fake-sysfs re-run passes 8/8, but that only tests the plumbing.
verdicts.rerun_numbers: wsl.exe -d Ubuntu -- python3 research/usb_cameras/naming/test_linux_fake_sysfs.py gives 8/8 PASS (original result file restored afterwards).

verdicts.claim: macOS: Apple documents uniqueID as persistent across reconnects and reboots; developers report it is locationID<<32|VID<<16|PID; an Apple media engineer said the pattern is kept for backward compatibility; users report swaps across reboots for identical devices in PCIe enclosures.
verdicts.reason: I opened all the sources and they support the wording. Apple's uniqueID doc: 'persists on one system across device connections and disconnections, application restarts, and reboots'. Thread 803759 has an 'Apple Staff, Media Engineer' saying 'We need to retain that pattern for backward compatibility', and ssmith_c (not Apple staff) says it 'has changed in the past, it might change at any time'. In thread 836715 the OP reports reboot swaps behind PCIe-in-Thunderbolt enclosures, built-in ports stable, and no Apple explanation. Nothing has been run on a Mac. My synthetic plist re-run passes 5/5.
verdicts.rerun_numbers: uv run --script research/usb_cameras/naming/test_macos_fake_ioreg.py gives 5/5 PASS (original result restored).

verdicts.claim: A camera with a usable serial keeps its Windows instance id (and MF/DShow paths) when moved to another port; serial-less cameras get new ones (untested for the serial case).
verdicts.reason: Correctly labelled untested. The C922 has only one instance in its history. The serial-less half is backed by history evidence (finding 3). The serial-keeps-id half rests only on the MS blog, which says the parent information is used only when there is no serial. The drafted workflow parses (PowerShell parser: 0 errors).
verdicts.rerun_numbers: None possible without a physical port move.

harness_bugs: No result file captures hub LastArrivalDate, so the 'hubs did not re-arrive' claim had no file evidence. The 2026-10-24T14:04Z values it cited are camera arrivals in the baseline dump. I confirmed it with Get-PnpDeviceProperty DEVPKEY_Device_LastArrivalDate on the 5 hubs. win_identity_dump.py should record port_chain[].LastArrivalDate.

The baseline snapshot (baseline_initial.json) has no mf_*/dshow_*/ffmpeg/camera_key fields, so the 18:14Z diff could not test their stability. That was closed by my re-run across the 18:48Z re-arrival.

camera_identity_list.json is raw PowerShell-redirected stdout (UTF-8 BOM, CRLF, bare list). It has none of the README-required fields (test, platform, hostname, utc_started, command, environment), and the 0.454 s timing is not stored anywhere; json.load() without utf-8-sig fails on it.
The finding cites '23/23 parser checks', but test_parsers.json contains 28/28. test_parsers.json also lacks utc_started.

Re-running win_identity_dump.py (without --out-dir), win_api_names.py (no --out-dir option at all), test_parsers.py and test_macos_fake_ioreg.py overwrites the cited evidence files in results/. Verification needs a backup/restore; I restored all originals and moved my api_names_history file to the scratchpad.
test_linux_fake_sysfs.json is written to results/linux/Gerald/ (the WSL hostname). That looks like a real-Linux-host result, though it is a fake-sysfs plumbing test.
The 'OpenCV index' columns come from cv2_enumerate_cameras.enumerate_cameras(), not from opening cv2.VideoCapture(index, backend). The index-to-camera equality is never measured.
drafted_test_issues: All 11 naming/*.py files parse (ast). linux_stability_workflow.sh and macos_stability_workflow.sh pass both bash -n and dash -n. I checked that the diff loop's '[ -f ] && set --' under set -eu does not abort in dash or bash --posix. The 3 .ps1 files parse with 0 errors in the PowerShell parser.

Result paths match the README: linux results/linux/$(hostname)/naming (shell) and socket.gethostname() (python), the same on Linux; macOS hostname -s vs socket.gethostname().split('.')[0], normally the same.

win_stability_workflow.ps1 looks for snapshots under $env:COMPUTERNAME, while win_identity_dump.py writes under socket.gethostname(). The case difference is harmless on NTFS, but COMPUTERNAME is the NetBIOS name, truncated to 15 characters. On a machine with a longer hostname the -Step diff would look in the wrong directory.
Linux and macOS collectors have only been run against a fake sysfs in WSL (8/8, re-run by me) and a synthetic ioreg plist (5/5, re-run by me). They are unverified on real hardware.
win_restart_test.py cannot produce a result while LogiTuneAgent.exe or RazerAppEngine.exe are running. Its header says to quit them first, and that note is correct.
result.corrected_summary:
I confirmed the core naming results on this Windows machine by re-running them. The identity dump (19:02Z), the API names (19:04Z) and 5 timed camera_identity runs were done under camlock, and the descriptors were re-parsed with my own parser, separate from usbdesc.py.

- **Serials:** only the C922 has an iSerialNumber (B76395EF), and Windows uses it as the instance id. The Kiyo Pro, C930e and Jieli have iSerialNumber=0 and get parent-hash&0&port ids.
- **PnP history:** the Kiyo has 3 instances/ContainerIds and the C930e has 2. The C930e's current instance was created today at 17:32Z.
- **ContainerId:** v5 for the serial camera, v1 (generated) for the others.
- **IgnoreHWSerNum:** none applies. There are 11 global values (VIDs 04E8/05C6), and the per-device keys hold only osvc=0000.
- **Descriptors:** the numbers are correct: bcdUVC 1.00, dwClockFrequency C922 300 MHz / others 30 MHz, max iso bandwidth C922 24.48 MB/s, C930e 24.576, Jieli 24.552, Kiyo 270.336 MB/s at SuperSpeed, and the format/frame counts. The claim that every camera's strings can be read is wrong: the Kiyo's string reads still fail with Errno 31 after two re-arrivals. Parser checks are 28/28, not 23/23.
- **Reconnect stability:** the 18:14Z re-arrival did not compare the MF/DShow/FFmpeg/camera_key fields, which were null in the baseline. A second unattributed re-arrival of all 4 cameras at 18:47:56-18:48:16Z (hubs still at 2026-10-24T14:04Z, checked by me) fills that gap. Diffing final_with_4th_camera against my re-run, only the USB address changed (20->24, 5->6, 22->25, 21->23). Instance ids, LocationPaths, ContainerId, KS/MF/DShow paths and indices, FFmpeg alternative names and camera_key all stayed the same. Neither event was a physical replug, port move or reboot, and their cause is unknown.
- **Restart test:** pnputil /restart-device remains inconclusive (4/4 exit 3010, LogiTuneAgent veto). DN_NEED_RESTART (0x100) is set.
- **API mapping:** the MF link is the KSCATEGORY_VIDEO_CAMERA interface, the DShow/FFmpeg path is the KSCATEGORY_CAPTURE interface, and the indices are reproducible (C922 MF 4 / DShow 0; 8 MF, 15 DShow). The OpenCV-index equality comes only from cv2_enumerate_cameras and was never checked by opening VideoCapture.
- **Friendly names:** generic names are confirmed ('USB Video Device' for the Kiyo, 'USB Camera' for the Jieli).
- **Key scheme:** camera_identity keys reproduce (1 serial key, 3 port keys) in 0.29-0.37 s including uv start-up (5 runs).
- **Speed and companion ports:** EX Speed reports only up to high speed and V2 is needed for SuperSpeed (documented by MS and seen on the Kiyo). The claim that a USB2-enumerated camera changes its port key is an untested inference.
- **Serial character rule:** the udev rule is confirmed from source. The Windows part is overstated: the cited MS blog says the characters are 'not allowed' (bugcheck risk), not that Windows ignores the serial.
- **Linux and macOS:** the cited sources say what is claimed. Both remain documented-untested; the fake-sysfs (8/8) and synthetic ioreg (5/5) re-runs only test the plumbing.
- **Still untested:** whether a serial camera keeps its instance id after a port move, and whether two identical serial-less cameras can be told apart.

The overall conclusion holds: use the serial when it is present, valid and unique, otherwise the port path. On Windows, LocationPaths is stable across same-port re-enumeration.

result.topic: Goal 2 timing verification: UVC PTS/SCR versus OS timestamps on Windows usbvideo (MF), plus the Linux and macOS drafts

verdicts.claim: usbvideo exposes UVC PTS/SCR via MF only when MetadataBufferSizeInKB0 is set on the interface's DeviceClasses '#GLOBAL\Device Parameters' key. With it, every C922/C930e sample carries a 40-byte item (Id=2 MetadataId_UsbVideoHeader, an 8-byte header plus 32-byte KSSTREAM_UVC_METADATA). MS doc says 24 bytes.
verdicts.reason: The measurable parts reproduce. Baseline_nometa_auto has 0/290 and 0/293 frames with metadata; meta_check1 has 142/142 and 138/138 with meta_len=40. My fresh run has 893/893 (C922) and 890/890 (C930e) at meta_len 40. The meta_hex starts 02000000 28000000. SDK ksmedia.h 6303-6320 and ks.h give 2x16-byte timestamps plus the 8-byte header. The MS uvc-extensions-1-5 page does say 'sizeof(KSCAMERA_METADATA_ITEMHEADER) + sizeof(KSTREAM_UVC_METADATA) or 24 bytes'. The registry has exactly six keys set to 5, all from the approved change. Three problems: (1) 'only through the MF pipeline' was never tested; no DirectShow or KS-direct attempt was made. (2) The cited MS uvc-camera-implementation-guide does not mention MetadataBufferSizeInKB anywhere; only the librealsense script supports that path. (3) The key sits under the port-dependent interface instance path. Unset siblings exist for other ports (e.g. C930e 8&16BE97FE, Kiyo a&149b2a0f), so the setting does not follow a camera to another port.
verdicts.rerun_numbers: vflash1: C922 893/893 frames meta_len=40, C930e 890/890; MF sample time == MFSampleExtension_DeviceTimestamp on 893/893 and 890/890

verdicts.claim: All Windows OS-side timestamps (MF sample time = DeviceTimestamp, host arrival, attr D06F8A46) lie on a 16.000 ms grid with an independent phase per stream (2.94, 5.94, 15.45 ms). Intervals are 16/32/48 ms. Periodic-fit jitter is 4.2-5.1 ms rms.
verdicts.reason: Re-running quantization_check on baseline_nometa_auto gives identical output: best grid 16.0 ms, concentration 0.999-1.000; mf_sample_time intervals are only 16/32/48 ms. On fresh data os_timestamp has concentration 1.0 on the 16 ms grid. My independent check (timing/scripts/verify_grid_phase.py) finds the absolute QPC phase deviation is only 23-52 us std, and phases differ per camera. The quoted phase values (2.94/5.94/15.45) appear in no evidence file. Phase is per session anyway: run1 OS phase C930e 12.69 / C922 7.69 ms; my run 8.45 / 14.45 ms. Caveat: for the C930e, analyze_frames' periodic fit locks onto 32.42 fps for host/os sources, so those jitter and drops_est numbers are partly artefacts. Only 1280x720@30 MJPEG on the Intel xHCI controllers was tested.
verdicts.rerun_numbers: vflash1 quantization: os_timestamp [16.0 ms, 1.000] both cams, host_arrival [16.0, 0.95]; grid phase dev std os_ts 24.9 us (C930e) / 22.8 us (C922); interval multiples {2:813, 3:70-74}; OS/arrival periodic jitter 4.26-4.73 ms rms

verdicts.claim: Screen-flash ground truth: UVC PTS via SCR has 0.22-0.72 ms per-frame error std on C922 and C930e, about 10x better than every OS timestamp (C922 4.1-4.8 ms, C930e 4.5-12.5 ms). This is close to the method floor (75 us synthetic).
verdicts.reason: Re-running flash_analyze on runs/flash1 reproduces flash_analysis.json exactly. Fresh run vflash1 (E=7.81 ms): C922 PTS routes 465-582 us, OS 4.50-4.66 ms (in range). C930e PTS routes 1.05-1.17 ms, outside the claimed range; OS 9.9-10.1 ms. Re-analysis of the unreported flash_verify_1 capture: C930e PTS-via-SCR 1.02-1.07 ms, OS 10.6-11.4 ms; C922 0.48-0.63 ms. The roughly 10x advantage over OS timestamps holds; the absolute sub-0.72 ms range does not hold for the C930e. The method also cannot attribute about 0.5 ms accuracy to PTS. verify_method.json and timing/VERIFY_method.md show seq_periodic_env (frame index + arrival envelope, no device timestamp) scores the same as PTS (C930e 531 vs 531 us, C922 584 vs 589 us). The tone-curve gamma is tuned to the reference source and changes PTS scores from 0.5 to 1.7 ms. Errors correlate with brightness fraction f (r = -0.76/+0.64), so the real-data floor is about 0.5 ms, not 75 us. The test therefore only bounds PTS error at roughly 0.5-1 ms. At E=1.95 ms the GT uses n=12 (C922) and n=20 (C930e) frames, and the window truncation bounds the error at about E/sqrt(6)=0.8 ms, so those numbers are weak.
verdicts.rerun_numbers: vflash1 vs-GT std (us): C922 pts_direct 465, via_scr 582, via_scr_lsq 538, os 4504, arrival 4601, d06f 4657; C930e via_scr 1048, via_scr_lsq 1068, pts_direct 1173, os 10140, arrival 9935. flash_verify_1 reanalysis: C930e via_scr_lsq 1023, os 11433; C922 pts_direct 482, via_scr_lsq 593, os 4737

verdicts.claim: Rolling-shutter readout over full height is C922 about 30.0 ms and C930e 27.3-28.5 ms.
verdicts.reason: The flash_rows re-run on flash1 reproduces the numbers exactly (29.995 / 28.532). The fresh run gives C922 30.52 ms (resid 0.58) and C930e 27.68 ms. flash_rows fits only offset vs row, but each row picks its own best column. For the C930e, block row and column are almost collinear (corr -0.96 in every run). A row+column fit gives a C930e row slope of 31.95-32.88 ms and a column term of 20-27 ms, so display scan-out and ROI geometry are confounded with readout. VERIFY_method.md says the same. The C922 number is robust: row+col fit 30.1-30.6 ms, row/col corr 0.12 to -0.65. The C930e value is uncertain by about 5 ms.
verdicts.rerun_numbers: vflash1: C922 30.52 ms (row+col fit 30.31), C930e 27.68 ms (row+col fit 32.88, col coeff 26.7); run1/exp-9/exp-6 C930e row+col fits 31.95/32.03/32.21 ms

verdicts.claim: C922 device SOF advances 884 counts per host second (confirms Linux UVC_QUIRK_INVALID_DEVICE_SOF for 046d:085c). PTS/STC are 300 MHz (-5.6 ppm vs QPC). STC-PTS is 32.99 +/- 0.14 ms. First-to-last-payload SCR difference is 1.55M ticks (5.2 ms).
verdicts.reason: analyze_frames re-run on flash1 is identical. Fresh run: usb_sof_ms_per_host_s 884.84, dev_sof_step 29.49 ms, STC-PTS 33.01 +/- 0.12 ms, eof-sof SCR 1.566M ticks. Linux v6.12 uvc_driver.c lines 2566-2573 list 046d:085c with UVC_QUIRK_INVALID_DEVICE_SOF, and uvc_video.c 591-598 has the C922 host-SOF substitution; I downloaded both to read them. The ppm vs QPC is not reproducible: +6.7 ppm in my run vs -5.6 ppm. The arrival-based rate estimator is good only to about +/-10 ppm over 30 s, so report the rate as '300 MHz within ~10 ppm'. Not in the claim: the C922 PTS period alternates 9.9126M / 10.0848M ticks (+/-0.27 ms; periodic residual 124-137 us), so its PTS has about 0.5 ms granularity.
verdicts.rerun_numbers: vflash1 C922: usb_sof_ms_per_host_s=884.84; pts_freq_vs_host=300,002,015 Hz (+6.7 ppm); stc_minus_pts 33.006 +/- 0.123 ms; eof_minus_sof_scr_stc 1,565,911 ticks; pts_period std 73,893 ticks

verdicts.claim: C930e: STC 30.0013 MHz (+41.6 ppm vs SOF, +44 ppm vs QPC); actual 30.085 fps; PTS periodic to 2.2 us rms; STC-PTS bimodal (median 31.0, p95 52.1, max 53.8 ms); arrival-based PTS mapping unreliable (5.7-7.4 ms in 2 of 3 runs); SCR identical in first and last payload.
verdicts.reason: These parts reproduce: 30.085 fps (30.0849), eof==sof SCR (0 ticks), and the unreliable arrival-envelope mapping (flash_verify_1 reanalysis 10.3 ms; mine 1.17 ms). These are run-specific: (a) the 2.2 us PTS periodicity. In my run the C930e PTS has recurring single-frame glitches: one PTS about 30,012 ticks (1.0 ms) early, then back, at frames 31, 85, 301, 355, 409 and so on. Periodic residual is 120 us rms, though p05-p95 is still 10-19 us. (b) The STC-PTS distribution: median 42.9, p95 58.5, max 60.5 ms in my run, so it varies by session over 30-60 ms. (c) The ppm figures: STC vs SOF +46.4 ppm (vs 41.6). STC vs QPC came out +13 ppm (vs 44), and that is inconsistent with device_vs_usb + usb_vs_host (= 44 ppm) in the same file. So the vs-QPC estimator is unreliable. The analyzer's device_vs_host_ppm (+393 run1, +163 mine) is plainly wrong.
verdicts.rerun_numbers: vflash1 C930e: fps via_scr 30.0849; stc_per_sof 30,001,391 Hz (+46.4 ppm); stc_freq_vs_host 30,000,398 Hz; pts_period 997,222 median, std 5,148 ticks (outliers 967,2xx / 1,027,2xx); pts periodic resid 120 us rms; stc_minus_pts median 42.88 p95 58.50 max 60.49 ms; eof-sof SCR 0

verdicts.claim: UVC 1.5 defines PTS as source clock at start of raw frame capture, and SCR (STC at first video data on bus plus 11-bit SOF) as constant within a frame. dwClockFrequency comes from Probe/Commit (the VC header field is deprecated). The C922 changes SCR within a frame.
verdicts.reason: Downloaded zip sha256 is 67ed3227...c1e9, matching the claim. The extracted spec text has the PTS definition 'source clock time in native device clock units when the raw frame capture begins', the Table 2-6 'STC must be captured when the first video data of a video frame is put on the USB bus' and 'SCR must remain constant for all payload transfers within a single video frame', and 'Use of this field has been deprecated' for the VC header dwClockFrequency. The measurement reproduces: PTS eof==sof is 1.0 for both cameras; C922 SCR differs by 1.566M ticks; C930e by 0. Note that analyze_frames never read dwClockFrequency (nominal_assumed=true).
verdicts.rerun_numbers: vflash1: eof_pts_equals_sof_pts_fraction 1.0 (both); C922 eof-sof SCR 1,565,911 ticks; C930e 0

verdicts.claim: Exposure dependence of row-0 offset: C922 -29.9/-37.7/-46.4 ms at E 1.95/7.81/15.6 ms suggests PTS marks end of exposure. C930e is non-monotonic. Inconclusive because of per-session mapping constants.
verdicts.reason: The status 'inconclusive' is appropriate. The fresh repeat at E=7.81 gives C922 d0 -38.2 ms (vs -37.67, reproducible to 0.5 ms), so the C922 trend (-16.5 ms for +13.7 ms of exposure) is fairly credible. The C930e moved 4.3 ms between sessions at the same exposure (-51.65 vs -47.38), larger than its exposure trend, so it is uninformative. d0 is also confounded by scan-out and ROI geometry (see the rolling-shutter verdict).

verdicts.claim: Synthetic validation: Linux end-point SCR mapping 258 us std, least squares 94 us (mean -3.6 us) with host SOF. The Windows-like case without host SOF has a +21 ms absolute error. Flash method floor 75 us; injected 1000 -> 1007 us, 4600 -> 4460 us.
verdicts.reason: Both self-tests re-run and reproduce exactly: 257.74 / 94.21 us, mean -3.60 us; windows_like envelope mean +21,416 us; flash 74.8 us floor, 1006.7, 4460.0. Caveats: the synthetic world matches the analyzers' models exactly, so the 75 us floor does not transfer to real data (about 0.5 ms; see VERIFY_method.md). The per_frame metric underestimates large errors (4600 injected -> 2383 recovered), but the claims correctly use vs_ground_truth. The 'Linux end-point' path is a Python re-implementation, not the kernel.
verdicts.rerun_numbers: via_scr_linux std 257.74 us mean -2.69; via_scr_lsq_linux std 94.21 mean -3.60; windows_like via_scr_lsq_envelope mean 21,416 us std 219.9; flash selftest 74.8 / 1006.7 / 4460.0 us

verdicts.claim: Linux (documented): V4L2 buffer timestamp is MONOTONIC/SOE but set at first-payload decode. hwtimestamps (default 0, 0644) rewrites it from PTS/SCR. The metadata node gives {u64 ns, u16 host SOF, header} without root.
verdicts.reason: No Linux run exists. I downloaded and read the cited v6.12 sources, and they support the text. uvc_queue.c 225-226: TIMESTAMP_MONOTONIC | TSTAMP_SRC_SOE. uvc_video.c 1184: the timestamp is set in uvc_video_decode_start from uvc_video_get_time(); 769: clock_update returns if !uvc_hw_timestamps_param. uvc_driver.c 33-34 and 2388: hwtimestamps 0644. uvcvideo.h 93-99: struct uvc_meta_buf {u64 ns; u16 sof; u8 length; u8 flags; buf[]}; uvc_video.c 1413-1417 fills ns and the host frame number. 'Without root' still depends on /dev/video* permissions (group video). The draft passes py_compile and prints 'self-test OK' on Windows.
verdicts.rerun_numbers: v4l2_uvc_timing.py --self-test -> 'self-test OK (python 3.12.13, AMD64)'

verdicts.claim: Restart incident: LogiTuneAgent and RazerAppEngine vetoed query-remove (Kernel-PnP 225). pnputil returned 3010 then 50, leaving DN_NEED_RESTART. Metadata later flows despite the flag. Kiyo fails every ReadSample with 0x8007001F.
verdicts.reason: The logs show 3010 (14:04) and then 50 (14:09, 14:12). The cited logs contain only LogiTuneAgent veto events. I queried the System log myself: Kernel-PnP 225 at 14:04:34 names RazerAppEngine.exe pid 35292 for the Kiyo MI_00, so the Razer part is true but not in the cited evidence. Further LogiTuneAgent vetoes occurred at 14:33 (pid 45784, not from this agent's logs). Right now all three MI_00 devnodes are 0x180200A with DN_NEED_RESTART set, and C922/C930e metadata flows (my run). The Kiyo again gave ReadSample hr=0x8007001f and 0 frames in my run. kiyo_check session.json records only errors=21, not the HRESULT. The MF_E_REBOOT_REQUIRED evidence exists only in other topics' files (bw_concurrency, mjpeg_mf_recheck, rust_nokhwa_capture), not in this topic's cited files.
verdicts.rerun_numbers: vflash1 capture.log: Kiyo 'ReadSample hr=0x8007001f', 0 frames; C922 893 frames/30.03 s, C930e 890/30.02 s; DevNodeStatus now 0x180200A (need_restart=True) for all three MI_00

verdicts.claim: macOS AVFoundation: CMSampleBuffer PTS is on the host time clock; UVC PTS/SCR are not exposed; frames are decoded. The draft checks synchronizationClock.
verdicts.reason: No sources are cited and nothing was run on macOS. avf_timing.py and run_macos_timing.sh pass py_compile and bash -n, and write to results/macos/<host>/timing/<utc>/ as the README requires.

harness_bugs: tools/analyze_frames.py: pts_freq_vs_host / device_vs_host_ppm come from OLS against host arrival and are biased by the C930e's latency regimes. They read +393 ppm (run1) and +163 ppm (vflash1) against an STC of about +44 ppm. stc_freq_vs_host is also unstable (+44 vs +13 ppm between runs) and contradicts device_vs_usb + usb_vs_host in the same file. Use an envelope fit or SOF-based rates, or drop these fields.

tools/analyze_frames.py: the periodic_fit periodogram locks onto 32.42 fps for the C930e's host_arrival/os_timestamp, so the jitter_rms and drops_est for those sources are artefacts. Prefer PTS slot gaps for drop counting.
tools/analyze_frames.py: dwClockFrequency is never read; nominal_hz is guessed (nominal_assumed=true).

timing/scripts/flash_analyze.py: gamma is tuned to minimise the reference source's own error, and the reference is the best-scoring source. That makes the best source's vs_ground_truth equal its own fit (circular). Use a fixed or independently calibrated tone curve and a device-timestamp-free reference (flash_verify_method.py already does this). The 75 us synthetic floor does not carry over to real data (about 0.5 ms).

timing/scripts/flash_rows.py: fits offset vs row only, but picks a different best column per row. For the C930e, row and column are collinear (r=-0.96), so readout is confounded with display scan-out and column gradient. Add a column term or use fixed-column blocks.

timing/scripts/quantization_check.py: does not output the grid phase, so the per-camera phases quoted in the claim (2.94/5.94/15.45 ms) have no evidence file. I added timing/scripts/verify_grid_phase.py, which reports absolute phase and interval multiples.
mf_uvc_timing session.json records only an error count, not the failing HRESULT (kiyo_check shows errors=21 only; 0x8007001F appears only in console capture.log).
Raw .mjpeg for every flash run (including my vflash1) lives only in the session scratchpad, so flash_analyze/flash_rows cannot be re-run from results/ alone once the scratchpad is cleaned.
drafted_test_issues: linux/v4l2_uvc_timing.py: py_compile OK and --self-test OK on Windows (struct and parser only). It is UNVERIFIED on Linux. It saves only a sample JPEG, not the full MJPEG stream with mjpeg_offset, so flash_analyze/flash_rows cannot run on Linux output (the author acknowledges this). Output path results/linux/<host>/timing/v4l2_uvc_timing/[<tag>/] matches the README.
linux/run_linux_timing.sh: bash -n OK. The optional hwtimestamps pass relies on sudo -n and is skipped without passwordless sudo. Unverified.

macos/avf_timing.py: py_compile OK; pins pyobjc 10.3.1. Writes results/macos/<host>/timing/<utc>/. Never run. session.synchronizationClock needs macOS 12.3+; I did not check the fallback on older macOS. It cannot confirm the 'decoded frames / no PTS-SCR' claims beyond listing attachments.
macos/run_macos_timing.sh: bash -n OK; unverified.

result.corrected_summary:
On Windows 11 usbvideo with MF, MJPEG 1280x720@30 and manual exposure/WB, the following were re-verified. My fresh camlock run is results/windows/Gerald/timing/verify_rerun_vflash1/, and I re-analysed the existing flash1 and flash_verify_1 captures.

(1) Setting MetadataBufferSizeInKB0=5 (registry, admin) on the interface's port-specific DeviceClasses key gives every C922/C930e sample a 40-byte MetadataId_UsbVideoHeader item with start-of-frame and end-of-frame PTS/SCR. The MS doc's '24 bytes' is wrong. The key does not follow a camera to another USB port. Exclusivity to MF was not tested.

(2) All OS-side timestamps (MF sample time = DeviceTimestamp = QPC, host arrival, attr D06F8A46) are quantised to a 16.000 ms grid, phase per stream and per session (phase scatter 23-52 us). Their error against screen-flash ground truth is 4.5-4.9 ms std for the C922 and 4.5-12.5 ms for the C930e (vflash1 10.1 ms).

(3) UVC PTS mapped to QPC (through SCR, or directly through an arrival envelope) is about 10x better. C922: 0.45-0.67 ms std in five sessions. C930e: 0.33-0.48 ms in the original three sessions but 1.02-1.17 ms in two later sessions. The flash method's own real-data floor is about 0.5 ms, and a timestamp-free frame-index model scores the same as PTS. So these numbers only bound PTS error at under about 0.5-1 ms; they do not measure it. The direct arrival-envelope mapping fails on the C930e (5.7-10.3 ms in 3 of 5 sessions), so the SCR route is needed there.

(4) Clocks. C922: PTS/STC at 300 MHz within about +/-10 ppm of QPC (sign not reproducible). Device SOF runs at 884-885 counts/s, consistent with Linux UVC_QUIRK_INVALID_DEVICE_SOF for 046d:085c (source checked). STC-PTS is 33.0 +/- 0.13 ms. SCR changes within a frame (1.55-1.57M ticks), against UVC 1.5. The PTS period alternates +/-0.27 ms. C930e: 30.085 fps (reproduced). STC is about +42-46 ppm vs USB SOF. STC-PTS varies by session over 30-60 ms. PTS is usually periodic to about 10-20 us, but with recurring single-frame 1.0 ms glitches in one session (residual 2.2 vs 120 us rms).

(5) Rolling-shutter readout over the full height: C922 30.0-30.6 ms (robust). C930e is 27-33 ms depending on whether a column/scan-out term is fitted, so it is not resolved.

(6) Whether PTS marks exposure start or end is unresolved. The C922 trend (reproducible to 0.5 ms) suggests end of exposure. The C930e's session-to-session offset shifts of about 4 ms make its data uninformative.

(7) Incident: pnputil restarts were vetoed by LogiTuneAgent and RazerAppEngine (System log Kernel-PnP 225). All three MI_00 devnodes still show DN_NEED_RESTART (0x180200A). The C922 and C930e stream with metadata. The Kiyo Pro still fails every ReadSample with 0x8007001F.

Linux and macOS claims are documented-only. The cited Linux v6.12 source lines check out. The drafts parse, but none has been run, and the Linux draft cannot feed the flash analysis because it does not save the full MJPEG stream.

Recommendation unchanged: use UVC PTS (with SCR or host-SOF mapping) and never the Windows OS timestamps for sync. Absolute and cross-camera offsets still need a host-SOF/QPC correlation (WinUSB/libusb or the Linux metadata node), and an LED or no-scan-out light source to measure them properly.

result.topic: Goal 3: USB isochronous bandwidth allocation control (research/usb_cameras/bandwidth/)
result.summary:
I built a Windows harness that needs no admin rights. It has four parts. (a) win_usb_topology.py reads hub IOCTLs to get each camera's controller, root port and hub, every VideoStreaming alt setting with its bytes per microframe, and the hub's live list of OPEN PIPES. The open-pipe list shows which alt setting usbvideo.sys selected while a stream runs, without ETW or admin. This is unambiguous for high-speed cameras; for SuperSpeed (Kiyo) it narrows to alt 1 or 2 only. (b) mf_multi_open.cpp opens N cameras through the Media Foundation SourceReader on their native types, with exposure fixed at -7 and white balance at 4500 K; previous values are restored after each run. It reports the HRESULT, fps and bytes/s for each camera. (c) run_concurrency.py runs batches of combinations under camlock and snapshots the open pipes while they stream. (d) hs_budget_model.py and headroom.py analyse the results offline.

A fourth camera appeared during the session: 4c4a:4a55 "USB Camera", which has a single 3x1023 B/microframe alt setting. It sits on the same Genesys 05e3:0610 USB 2.0 hub as the C930e. That gave a real shared 480 Mb/s link to test on.

Headline results:
1. For MJPEG, usbvideo reserves far more than the stream uses. C930e MJPEG 1280x720@30 gets alt 11 (3072 B/microframe = 24.6 MB/s) but uses 4.06 MB/s (6.0x). 640x480@30 gets alt 10 (21.5 MB/s) for 1.75 MB/s (12.3x). For the C930e, MJPEG requests the same alt as YUY2 at every mode tested. C922 MJPEG 720p30 gets alt 9: 15.9 MB/s reserved for 3.63 MB/s used (4.4x). The generic camera always takes 24.55 MB/s, even for 0.35 MB/s of MJPEG at 640x480 (70x).
2. On the shared hub, C930e alt 11 plus the generic camera fails. The camera started second gets HRESULT 0x800718CF ("A camera interface doesn't have the desired bandwidth for data transfer.") on its first ReadSample. The first-started stream wins and keeps full fps; the loser gets no frames rather than a lower frame rate.
3. The pass/fail threshold is C930e alt 8 (2x800) plus the generic camera passing, and alt 9 (2x992) plus the generic camera failing. A model built from USB 2.0 sec. 5.11.3 (worst-case bit stuffing, 80% periodic limit, sec. 5.6.4) predicts all 14 shared-hub outcomes correctly: 75.2% of the microframe passes, 81.1% fails.
4. Cameras on different root ports of the same xHCI do not compete. C922 alt 11 and C930e alt 11 streamed together (98.6% if they had shared a link).

Source-level findings (Linux mainline 21a7f44f, libuvc d07de4fa): UVC_QUIRK_FIX_BANDWIDTH (quirks=128) has applied ONLY to uncompressed formats since v2.6.32 (commit a2e35af6c756, 2009). So it should do nothing for MJPEG on any modern kernel, which contradicts the user's experience. The drafted Linux compare test checks this directly. Other Linux facts from source:
- The quirks parameter is 0644, global (not per camera), and read at probe time, so a root write plus unbind/bind should apply it.
- USBDEVFS_DISCONNECT has no capability check, so with a one-time udev rule libusb/libuvc can detach uvcvideo and pick the alt setting with no root at run time.
- Upstream libuvc picks the first alt with bytes >= ctrl.dwMaxPayloadTransferSize. An app can overwrite that field between uvc_get_stream_ctrl_format_size and uvc_start_streaming to get a smaller alt, without patching libuvc.
- libuvc's default buffers (100 transfers x 32 packets x 3072 B, about 9.8 MB per camera) exceed Linux's 16 MB default usbfs_memory_mb limit at two cameras, so build with LIBUVC_NUM_TRANSFER_BUFS=10.

macOS: libusb detach needs root or the com.apple.vm.device-access entitlement. Windows: I found no documented control over usbvideo's alt-setting choice; WinUSB plus libusb is the only app-level route.

Verdict: the headroom is real and large, typically 3-12x for MJPEG on Logitech cameras and up to 70x on the generic camera. headroom.py estimates 6 C930e 720p30 MJPEG cameras per high-speed root port at 1.5x margin, versus 1 as Windows reserves it. Recovering it requires libusb/libuvc forced alt settings, on Windows via WinUSB (phase 2). Whether cameras tolerate the smaller alt is not yet tested anywhere.

Not done: the one allowed UAC prompt for an ETW USB trace was cancelled by the user, so the probe/commit dwMaxPayloadTransferSize on Windows and the Kiyo's SuperSpeed alt remain unmeasured. The Kiyo Pro became unusable through MF during the session (0x8007001F).

findings.claim: Linux mainline uvcvideo applies UVC_QUIRK_FIX_BANDWIDTH (0x80) only to uncompressed formats: uvc_fixup_video_ctrl tests `!(format->flags & UVC_FMT_FLAG_COMPRESSED) && quirks & UVC_QUIRK_FIX_BANDWIDTH && num_altsetting > 1`, and MJPEG formats get UVC_FMT_FLAG_COMPRESSED (uvc_driver.c 'case UVC_VS_FORMAT_MJPEG: format->flags = UVC_FMT_FLAG_COMPRESSED; format->bpp = 0'). The restriction came from commit a2e35af6c756 ('uvcvideo: Ignore the FIX_BANDWIDTH for compressed video', 2009-11-07; in v2.6.32, not in v2.6.31). The quirk itself was added by 50144aeeb702 (v2.6.30). So quirks=128 can have changed the MJPEG bandwidth request only on 2.6.30/2.6.31. On any modern kernel it should be a no-op for MJPEG streams; this contradicts the user's experience and needs the drafted compare test. Later changes: 9bb7262de9c0 (minimum 1024 B), 9e3d55fbd160 (v6.11, SuperSpeed math), 9764401bf6f8 (v6.17, clamps an oversized request to the endpoint max instead of failing).
findings.command: gh api graphql blame of drivers/media/usb/uvc/uvc_video.c at torvalds/linux 21a7f44fd0765fcc5194130b28767786eba1d1e7; gh api repos/torvalds/linux/compare/v2.6.31...a2e35af6c756 (ahead) and v2.6.32...a2e35af6c756 (behind). Test to run: sudo env PATH=$PATH uv run --script research/usb_cameras/bandwidth/linux/uvc_bw_probe.py compare --mode MJPG:1280x720@30 --mode YUYV:640x480@30
findings.numbers: FIX_BANDWIDTH: in v2.6.30-2.6.31 only for compressed formats; uncompressed-only from v2.6.32 to master (2026)

findings.claim: Linux uvcvideo alt-setting selection (uvc_video_start_transfer): bandwidth = stream->ctrl.dwMaxPayloadTransferSize (0 is treated as 1). It loops over all altsettings and picks the one with the smallest psize >= bandwidth (usb_endpoint_max_periodic_payload; first such alt since 323666d1b323). If none fits it returns -EIO. uvc_probe_video retries PROBE with min/max compression parameters only when dwMaxPayloadTransferSize > maxpsize. The 323666d1b323 commit message states that Windows 10 picks the first alternate setting (from USB sniffing).
findings.command: source read: uvc_video.c lines 2042-2107 and 440-480 at 21a7f44f

findings.claim: The uvcvideo 'quirks' parameter is module_param_named(quirks, uvc_quirks_param, uint, 0644), so root can write /sys/module/uvcvideo/parameters/quirks at runtime. It is read only in uvc_probe (dev->quirks = uvc_quirks_param == -1 ? info->quirks : uvc_quirks_param), so it should take effect on the next probe, e.g. echo <intf> > /sys/bus/usb/drivers/uvcvideo/unbind then bind. It is global: it REPLACES the per-device table quirks of every camera probed while set. A per-device route exists via /sys/bus/usb/drivers/uvcvideo/new_id 'vid pid class refvid refpid': usb_store_new_id copies driver_info from the referenced uvc_ids entry, e.g. 0ac8:3410 = uvc_quirk_fix_bandwidth. All of these need root and none affect MJPEG.
findings.command: source read uvc_driver.c (lines 2214-2215, 2505, 2523-2525, 2847-2912) and drivers/usb/core/driver.c usb_store_new_id at 21a7f44f; drafted test: uvc_bw_probe.py compare (writes quirks, rebinds, checks dmesg 'Forcing device quirks to 0x80')

findings.claim: No root is needed at run time to take a camera away from uvcvideo on Linux. usbfs proc_ioctl USBDEVFS_DISCONNECT calls usb_driver_release_interface with no capability check (only privileges_dropped/connected/state checks), so read-write access to /dev/bus/usb/BBB/DDD is enough. A one-time udev rule can grant that: TAG+=uaccess matched on ID_USB_INTERFACES, the same idiom systemd uses for PTP cameras '*:060101:*'. The rule must sort before 73-seat-late.rules. Also, usbfs buffers are capped by usbfs_memory_mb (default 16 MB, 0644, root to change).
findings.command: source read drivers/usb/core/devio.c (proc_ioctl ~2318-2370, usbfs_memory_mb 134-160) at 21a7f44f; systemd rules.d at 2336319d
findings.numbers: usbfs_memory_mb default 16

findings.claim: Upstream libuvc (d07de4fa) chooses the alt setting in uvc_stream_start. config_bytes_per_packet = strmh->cur_ctrl.dwMaxPayloadTransferSize; it walks the altsettings in descriptor order (assuming sizes increase) and takes the FIRST whose bytes/packet (HS: (wMaxPacketSize&0x7ff)*(mult+1); SS: wBytesPerInterval) >= that value, else UVC_ERROR_INVALID_MODE. uvc_stream_ctrl() COMMITs the caller's struct and copies it into cur_ctrl without re-reading. So an app that overwrites ctrl.dwMaxPayloadTransferSize after uvc_get_stream_ctrl_format_size() and before uvc_start_streaming() gets a smaller alt with no libuvc patch, but only alts >= the override. Defaults: LIBUVC_NUM_TRANSFER_BUFS=100 (20 on macOS) and LIBUVC_PACKETS_PER_TRANSFER_MAX=32, so a 3072 B/microframe stream queues 100x32x3072 = 9.8 MB of iso buffers, beyond the 16 MB Linux usbfs default at two cameras. Both are CMake cache options in upstream CMakeLists. Minor upstream bug: the SS companion branch breaks on the first endpoint without checking bEndpointAddress.
findings.command: source read libuvc src/stream.c lines 406-423, 1150-1260; include/libuvc/libuvc_internal.h 226-251 at d07de4fa23905ee8cac06f5d24b2a03d42a3b363. Draft compiles against libuvc headers (MSVC /Zs syntax check, exit 0)
findings.numbers: 9.8 MB of iso buffers per 3072-B/microframe camera at default libuvc settings vs 16 MB usbfs default

findings.claim: macOS: libusb 1.0.30 darwin_detach_kernel_driver captures the whole device. It does so only if the process has the com.apple.vm.device-access entitlement (then IOServiceAuthorize) or euid==0; otherwise it returns LIBUSB_ERROR_ACCESS ('USB device capture requires either an entitlement (com.apple.vm.device-access) or root privilege'). Apple's entitlement page describes it as a key for apps that capture USB devices for a guest OS. So libuvc on macOS needs sudo or that entitlement; there is no udev-like one-time grant. AVFoundation exposes no alt-setting or bandwidth control (no API found; the drafted AVF test records OS default behaviour only).
findings.command: source read libusb-1.0.30/libusb/os/darwin_usb.c lines 2860-2945 (tarball fetched by the libusb agent into scratchpad downloads/libusb-1.0.30)

findings.claim: Windows: Microsoft's driver docs (stream/ and usbcon/ sections, searched) document no way for an application to choose or cap the isochronous alt setting usbvideo.sys uses. The USB docs describe alt setting and isochronous pipe selection only for client drivers (URB/WDF) and WinUSB. The only app-level route found is to replace usbvideo with WinUSB for that camera (phase 2) and use libusb/libuvc.
findings.command: gh search code against MicrosoftDocs/windows-driver-docs for dwMaxPayloadTransferSize (0 hits), 'alternate setting' and 'bandwidth' under windows-driver-docs-pr/stream

findings.claim:
Topology on Gerald:
- C922 (046d:085c) is high-speed on root port 1 of the Intel USB 3.20 xHCI (PCI DEV_7A60).
- C930e (046d:0843) and the generic 'USB Camera' (4c4a:4a55) are high-speed on ports 4 and 3 of the same Genesys 05e3:0610 USB 2.0 hub (chained 05e3:0610 -> root port 13 of DEV_7A60). These two SHARE one 480 Mb/s upstream link.
- Razer Kiyo Pro (1532:0e05) is SuperSpeed (V2 flags) behind a 05e3:0625 USB 3 hub on the separate Intel USB 3.10 xHCI (DEV_1138).
The legacy CONNECTION_INFORMATION_EX Speed field reports 'high' for the SuperSpeed Kiyo; the V2 flags are needed.
findings.command: uv run --script research/usb_cameras/bandwidth/win_usb_topology.py
findings.numbers: 4 UVC cameras, 2 controllers, 1 shared HS hub link (C930e + 4c4a:4a55)

findings.claim:
VideoStreaming alt settings (bytes per 125 us service interval, read from the config descriptor through the hub):
- C922 alts 1-11 = 192, 384, 512, 640, 800, 944, 1280 (2x640), 1600 (2x800), 1984 (2x992), 2688 (3x896), 3060 (3x1020).
- C930e: same list, but alt 11 = 3072 (3x1024).
- Generic 4c4a:4a55: a single streaming alt 1 = 3069 (3x1023), so it always reserves the HS maximum.
- Kiyo Pro (SS): alt 1 = 3072 (wBytesPerInterval, bMaxBurst 0, Mult 3), alt 2 = 33792 (bMaxBurst 10, Mult 3 = 270 MB/s).
The Linux draft's descriptor parser reproduces exactly these tables from the same raw bytes.
findings.command: uv run --script research/usb_cameras/bandwidth/win_usb_topology.py ; uv run --script research/usb_cameras/bandwidth/linux/uvc_bw_probe.py selftest --topology-json research/usb_cameras/results/windows/Gerald/bw_topology/topology.json
findings.numbers: generic camera 3069 B/microframe fixed; Kiyo alt2 33792 B/125us

findings.claim: Without admin or ETW, you can see which alt setting usbvideo.sys selected: while a stream runs, IOCTL_USB_GET_NODE_CONNECTION_INFORMATION_EX on the parent hub lists the device's open pipes (endpoint descriptor of the active alt). When idle only the VC interrupt pipe is open. For high-speed cameras every alt has a distinct wMaxPacketSize, so the match is unique. For the SuperSpeed Kiyo, alt 1 and alt 2 share wMaxPacketSize 0x400 and differ only in the companion descriptor, which the pipe list omits, so the result is ambiguous ([1,2]).
findings.command: uv run --script research/usb_cameras/tools/camlock.py -- uv run --script research/usb_cameras/bandwidth/run_concurrency.py --batch b02_c922_alt_by_mode --seconds 5 --exposure -7 --wb 4500 --combo "mjpg_1280x720_30|vid_046d&pid_085c:MJPG:1280x720@30" ... (full combo list in the JSON 'command' field)

findings.claim: Windows/usbvideo reserves several times more isochronous bandwidth for MJPEG than the stream uses, because cameras request it in dwMaxPayloadTransferSize. For the C930e, MJPEG requests the same alt as YUY2 at the same size and fps (352x288@30: alt 6 for both; 640x480@30: alt 10 for both; 1280x720@15 MJPEG: alt 11). This means the C930e asks for uncompressed-equivalent bandwidth for MJPEG. YUY2 reservations are tight (ratio 1.2-1.5).
findings.command: uv run --script research/usb_cameras/bandwidth/headroom.py (after the b02/b03/b04/b06 batches run via camlock + run_concurrency.py, exposure -7, wb 4500)

findings.claim: On the shared USB 2.0 hub link, two cameras whose reserved alts exceed the link's periodic budget cannot stream together. The camera that starts second fails on its first MF ReadSample with HRESULT 0x800718CF ('A camera interface doesn't have the desired bandwidth for data transfer.'). Which camera loses depends only on start order: with a 2.5 s stagger, the C930e started first makes the generic camera fail, and the reverse also holds. The winner keeps full frame rate. No fps degradation was observed in any combination that fit; failure is all-or-nothing at stream start.
findings.command: uv run --script research/usb_cameras/tools/camlock.py -- uv run --script research/usb_cameras/bandwidth/run_concurrency.py --batch b07_shared_hub_threshold_staggered --seconds 4 --exposure -7 --wb 4500 --stagger-ms 2500 --combo "c930e_alt8_then_gen|vid_046d&pid_0843:MJPG:640x480@15;vid_4c4a&pid_4a55:MJPG:1280x720@30" --combo "c930e_alt9_then_gen|vid_046d&pid_0843:MJPG:640x360@30;vid_4c4a&pid_4a55:MJPG:1280x720@30" ... (8 combos, see JSON)
findings.numbers:
Pass/fail with the generic camera (3x1023) on the shared link:
- C930e alt 6 (944), 7 (2x640), 8 (2x800) + generic: both stream
- C930e alt 9 (2x992), 10 (3x896), 11 (3x1024) + generic: second-started fails
HRESULT 0x800718CF

findings.claim: The shared-link pass/fail results match the USB 2.0 high-speed periodic budget. The model: HS iso IN transaction time = 38*8*2.083 + 2.083*floor(3.167 + 1.1667*8*bytes) ns (USB 2.0 sec. 5.11.3, worst-case bit stuffing, Host_Delay=0), with the limit at 80% of a 125 us microframe (sec. 5.6.4: 'High-speed endpoints can allocate at most 80% of a microframe for periodic transfers'). It predicts all 14 observed shared-hub combinations correctly: passing pairs used <= 75.2%, failing pairs >= 81.1%. Corollaries: two maximum-alt HS cameras (98.6%) can never share one HS link, and the fixed-alt generic camera alone uses 49.3% of the link. The 75.2% / 81.1% bracket is consistent with the 80% limit but does not pin down the host's exact formula.
findings.command: uv run --script research/usb_cameras/bandwidth/hs_budget_model.py
findings.numbers: 14/14 agree; per-transaction: 1024 B = 20546 ns, 1023 B = 20528 ns, 992 B = 19926 ns, 800 B = 16193 ns; passing max 75.2%, failing min 81.1%

findings.claim: Cameras on different root ports of the same Intel xHCI do not share HS bandwidth. Two pairs that would exceed one link's budget streamed simultaneously at full rate: C922 alt 11 + C930e alt 11 (root port 1 vs root port 13 via hub), and C922 alt 9 + the generic camera. This is consistent with xHCI budgeting periodic bandwidth per root-hub port. Linux >= 6.16 exposes per-root-port available bandwidth via debugfs port_bandwidth/{SS,HS,FS}_BW (commit 59d50e53e070, xHCI 'Get Port Bandwidth'); the Linux draft reads it.
findings.command: uv run --script research/usb_cameras/tools/camlock.py -- uv run --script research/usb_cameras/bandwidth/run_concurrency.py --batch b08_cross_rootport_and_kiyo --seconds 5 --exposure -7 --wb 4500 --stagger-ms 2000 --combo "c922_alt11_c930e_alt11_diff_rootports|vid_046d&pid_085c:MJPG:1920x1080@30;vid_046d&pid_0843:MJPG:1920x1080@30" ...
findings.numbers: C922 7.12 MB/s @30.02 fps + C930e 5.76 MB/s @30.08 fps simultaneously, both alt 11; four cameras (C922 alt 11, C930e alt 8, generic alt 1) streamed together, with the Kiyo failing for an unrelated reason

findings.claim: Headroom that an app-chosen alt setting could recover (estimate only; not tested whether the cameras tolerate smaller alts). For the C930e MJPEG 1280x720@30, the largest frame seen x fps needs alt 4 (640 B/microframe) at 1x and alt 5 (800) at 1.5x margin. That is 6 cameras per HS root port at 1.5x margin versus 1 as Windows reserves it. Other cameras per port at 1.5x margin: C922 720p30 MJPEG 6 (vs 2 reserved); C930e 1080p30 MJPEG 3 (vs 1). The generic camera cannot be reduced: it has no smaller alt setting.
findings.command: uv run --script research/usb_cameras/bandwidth/headroom.py
findings.numbers: C930e 720p30 MJPEG: 508 B/microframe average vs 3072 reserved; min alt x1/x1.5/x2 = 4/5/7

findings.claim:
System events observed during testing (not caused by this agent):
- From about 14:05 to 14:13, every USB camera failed MF activation with MF_E_REBOOT_REQUIRED (0xC00D7167). This coincided with another agent having set MetadataBufferSizeInKB0=5 under the cameras' device-interface keys; it cleared after the devices were restarted.
- From about 14:29 on, the Razer Kiyo Pro fails ReadSample with 0x8007001F (ERROR_GEN_FAILURE) on most opens. One MJPEG 720p30 open in a later retry streamed (2.68 MB/s), but that result file was overwritten by a later failing run.
So the Kiyo's SuperSpeed alt choice remains unmeasured.
findings.command: see 'command' fields in the JSON files
findings.numbers: 0xC00D7167 (MF_E_REBOOT_REQUIRED), 0x8007001F

findings.claim: An ETW USB trace (UCX/USBHUB3/USBXHCI with Default+FullDataBusTrace, per Microsoft's logman how-to) would have shown the VS_PROBE dwMaxPayloadTransferSize and the Kiyo's SuperSpeed alt. The single allowed UAC prompt was cancelled by the user, so no trace was captured and nothing was changed.
findings.command: uv run --script research/usb_cameras/bandwidth/etw/etw_capture.py --name etw01 -- --batch etw01_probe_commit ...

drafted_tests.run: uv run --script research/usb_cameras/bandwidth/linux/uvc_bw_probe.py list ; ... ramp --mode MJPG:1280x720@30 --seconds 8 ; sudo env "PATH=$PATH" uv run --script research/usb_cameras/bandwidth/linux/uvc_bw_probe.py compare --mode MJPG:1280x720@30 --mode YUYV:640x480@30
drafted_tests.measures: For each camera: the VS alt setting uvcvideo selected (sysfs bAlternateSetting + endpoint while streaming) and how many cameras stream concurrently (STREAMON errno, e.g. ENOSPC; fps; invalid JPEG; V4L2_BUF_FLAG_ERROR). 'compare' (root) repeats with quirks=-1 and quirks=128 after unbind/bind, captures uvcvideo trace=0x400 dmesg lines ('Device requested N B/frame bandwidth', 'Selecting alternate setting'), and reads xHCI debugfs port_bandwidth on kernels >= 6.16. It then restores quirks/trace and rebinds. It directly tests the source-based prediction that quirks=128 does not change MJPEG. UNVERIFIED (descriptor parser self-tested on Windows data only).
drafted_tests.needs: 64-bit Linux, uvcvideo, >= 2 UVC cameras behind ONE USB 2.0 hub, access to /dev/video*; root for 'compare'. Writes results/linux/<host>/bw_probe/*.json

drafted_tests.measures: Builds upstream libuvc d07de4fa with LIBUVC_NUM_TRANSFER_BUFS=10 and the test program. Runs (1) the camera-requested alt for 1..N cameras and (2) forced smaller alts (0.5x, 0.25x of dwMaxPayloadTransferSize, and 1024 B) for all cameras. Per camera it records the requested and used dwMaxPayloadTransferSize, the alt chosen, the start result, fps, bytes/s, invalid MJPEG frames and sequence gaps. Shows whether MJPEG survives smaller alts and how many cameras then fit, as a normal user on Linux (one-time udev rule). On macOS it runs once without and once with sudo. UNVERIFIED (MSVC syntax/type check only).

For the WinUSB/libuvc phase on Gerald:
1. The C930e (046d:0843, alts 1-11 = 192, 384, 512, 640, 800, 944, 1280, 1600, 1984, 2688, 3072 B/microframe) shares the Genesys 05e3:0610 USB 2.0 hub link with the generic 4c4a:4a55 (single alt 1 = 3x1023, stays on usbvideo, 49.3% of a microframe). Under usbvideo, C930e MJPEG 720p30 takes alt 11 and the pair cannot coexist (0x800718CF).
2. With the C930e on WinUSB, use the libusb agent's uvc_capture_test --alt N / --min-packet-bytes (or upstream libuvc with the ctrl.dwMaxPayloadTransferSize override, see bandwidth/libuvc_forced_alt/uvc_multi_forced_alt.c, which compiles against libusb/build headers). Start the generic camera through MF first: run_concurrency.py with --combo "gen|vid_4c4a&pid_4a55:MJPG:1280x720@30" in a parallel process.
3. Sweep C930e MJPEG 1280x720@30 over alts 3, 4, 5, 7, 8 and record: valid-JPEG fraction, fps, sequence gaps, the PROBE dwMaxPayloadTransferSize, and whether the alt is accepted next to the generic camera. Model predictions (hs_budget_model.py) for alts 3-8 with the generic camera: alt 3 = 57.8%, alt 4 = 59.8%, alt 5 = 62.2%, alt 7 = 70.2%, alt 8 = 75.2% (all fit); alt 9 and up fail. headroom.py says the measured stream needs about 508 B/microframe on average (alt 4 at 1x, alt 5 at 1.5x of the largest frame).
4. Also log the C930e's PROBE dwMaxPayloadTransferSize for MJPEG 640x480@30 and 1280x720@30. Windows picks alts 10 and 11 for these, so the expected values are 1985-2688 and 2689-3072, assuming Windows picks the smallest sufficient alt.
5. If possible, try lowering wCompQuality in PROBE to see whether the camera lowers its own request.
6. Use win_usb_topology.py --pipes-only while streaming to confirm the alt that WinUSB/libusb actually set.

verdicts.claim: An unprivileged process can use IOCTL_USB_START_TRACKING_FOR_TIME_SYNC and IOCTL_USB_GET_FRAME_NUMBER_AND_QPC_FOR_TIME_SYNC on both xHCI controllers. These return frame/microframe and QPC at 1 µs accuracy, exactly 1250 ticks per microframe, with ~20 µs latency. Past frames to -10 work; -500 and future frames fail; hubs fail. This lets each frame's SCR SOF be mapped to QPC.
verdicts.reason: The API behaviour is confirmed and reproduces: unelevated access works, the 32-bit frame mod 2048 equals the hardware frame, past -10 works, -500, future and 11-bit inputs give error 87, and all 9 hub interfaces give 87. The accuracy reading is wrong in two ways. (1) Microsoft's docs say both QPC outputs are 'a value predicted by the USB driver stack'. A residual of exactly 0 against frames*8+uframes x 1250 therefore only shows the driver's linear model. It says nothing about how accurately the model tracks the real SOF. Each run spanned only ~0.34 s, too short to see any drift correction. (2) The IOCTL page says PredictedAccuracyInMicroSeconds 'indicates accuracy in 125-microseconds unit' when a frame boundary was encountered, so the reported '1' may mean 125 µs, not 1 µs. Also, in both the original and the rerun, one sample on the 8086:1138 controller returned a microframe-start QPC after the IOCTL had already returned (original +7.2 µs, rerun +2.2 µs). That is impossible for a measured microframe start and contradicts ±1 µs. Separately, the claim that the SCR SOF can be mapped to QPC is untested: no camera was streamed, and whether the camera's 11-bit SOF equals the host hw_frame is an open question. The 'ticks, not microseconds' observation is consistent with the 10 MHz QPF and 1250 ticks/µframe, and the docs do say 'microseconds'.

The disassembly shows get_precise_timestamp_freq calls QPF into [rsp+38h] and returns without a store through rcx. get_host_time_us calls QPF into [rsp+30h] and then does idiv on qword [rsp+30h], so the same slot is used. result.json has 3/3 sentinels unchanged and 5/5 get_host_time_us results equal to 101528975397. verdicts.claim: WinUSB on the composite parent is the safer target for libusb (documented-untested).
verdicts.reason: libusb-1.0.30 windows_winusb.c:1532-1543 looks up DeviceInterfaceGUIDs, then DeviceInterfaceGUID, and logs 'no DeviceInterfaceGUID registered' if neither exists. The local C:\Windows\INF\winusb.inf (UTF-16) WINUSB.AddReg writes only DevLoader and NTMPDriver; only the ADB model writes DeviceInterfaceGUIDs. So an inbox install on MI_00 would not be discoverable by libusb as a usbccgp function. This is still documented reasoning, not a test.

verdicts.claim: libusb on WinUSB requires the isochronous transfer length to be a multiple of MaximumBytesPerInterval*8/interval at high speed (documented-untested).
verdicts.reason: libusb-1.0.30 windows_winusb.c:3643-3651 matches: it returns INVALID_PARAM with 'length of isoch buffer must be a multiple of the MaximumBytesPerInterval * 8 / Interval'. The claim that libuvc's 32 packets satisfy this depends on the packet size equalling MaximumBytesPerInterval. That was not checked, and --min-packet-bytes could break it.

verdicts.claim: On macOS 12+, libusb's detach returns ACCESS without root or the com.apple.vm.device-access entitlement. libuvc then does not claim. Issue #1014 was closed as a known limitation (documented-untested).
verdicts.reason: darwin_usb.c:2879 and 2929-2934 contain the entitlement check, and geteuid()!=0 returns LIBUSB_ERROR_ACCESS with the quoted warning. libuvc HEAD device.c:1004-1013 claims only on SUCCESS, NOT_FOUND or NOT_SUPPORTED. Issue #1014 is closed, titled '...no real solution, this is a macOS limitation'. In it, Apple DTS says the entitlement is for VM apps and osy says command-line apps cannot hold it. Still untested on a Mac.

verdicts.claim: On Linux, USBDEVFS_DISCONNECT needs only rw on the usbfs node, so a udev rule removes runtime sudo. Mainline applies FIX_BANDWIDTH only to uncompressed formats (documented-untested).
verdicts.reason: Current torvalds/master devio.c proc_ioctl (l.2318-2330) checks only ps->privileges_dropped and connected() before the USBDEVFS_DISCONNECT case. uvc_video.c:229 gates FIX_BANDWIDTH on !(format->flags & UVC_FMT_FLAG_COMPRESSED). uvc_driver.c:430-431 sets UVC_FMT_FLAG_COMPRESSED for V4L2_PIX_FMT_MJPEG, which confirms MJPEG is excluded. This is source-only. The open question about the user's quirks=128 experience with MJPEG remains and is significant for the bandwidth topic.

Hostname casing is inconsistent. The PowerShell scripts use $env:COMPUTERNAME ('GERALD') and the Python scripts use socket.gethostname() ('Gerald'). On Windows both land in results/windows/Gerald, but the JSON hostname fields disagree, and it would split directories on a case-sensitive filesystem.

In Ubuntu 24.04, libuvc's FindLibUSB prints 'libusb-1.0 could not be found using pkgconfig' even though build_unix.sh's own pkg-config check passes. The build succeeds only because the wrapper provides LibUSB::LibUSB. The same path on macOS/Homebrew is untested.

The phase-2 Windows chain (run_elevated install, verify -Stream, phase2_windows.ps1, rollback) has never run. The rollback depends on the C930e staying on port 1-13.1.4, because its instance ID is port-bound.
result.corrected_summary:
Confirmed by re-run:
- **Windows build.** build_windows.ps1 exits 0. libusb 1.0.30 and libuvc d07de4fa build Static-only with MSVC through three header shims and no libuvc source edits. The rebuild gives 11 warnings, all from libuvc headers or diag.c (the original log predates the test_payload_timing target and shows 10). build_info.json wrongly lists a stale uvc.dll left over from an earlier 'Both' build.
- **Linux build.** In Docker (Ubuntu 24.04, gcc 13.3, libusb 1.0.27) there are 0 gcc warnings and 1 CMake FindLibUSB warning. The patch unit test passes 23/23, and --list sees 0 devices.
- **Upstream libuvc audit.** Confirmed against the HEAD source: PTS and SCR are never exposed per frame, the SOF is never read (@todo at stream.c:797), capture_time is never set, and capture_time_finished is CLOCK_MONOTONIC at buffer swap. The patch's synthetic test passes 23/23 on Windows and Linux.
- **Python streamer.** Its unit test passes 24/24.
- **Enumeration on usbvideo.** Re-run under camlock: libusb sees 4 UVC devices (C930e, C922, Kiyo Pro, 4c4a:4a55) and can open none (LIBUSB_ERROR_NOT_FOUND, exit 3).
  - The C922 serial B76395EF equals its Windows instance-ID suffix.
  - The Kiyo Pro and C930e have iSerialNumber=0, and their instance IDs carry port suffixes. The C930e's stale &0&1 instance suggests the ID changes with the port, but no controlled reconnect test was done.
  - The Kiyo product string read without opening was null in the re-run.
  - pyuvc 1.0.8 behaves as claimed: it imports, lists every device as 'unknown', gives OpenError 'Entity not found', and bundles libusb 1.0.26.11724.
- **Descriptor values.** Re-run, Python implementation only:

| Camera | Isochronous alt settings (bytes per 125 µs) |
|---|---|
| C930e | 192, 384, 512, 640, 800, 944, 1280, 1600, 1984, 2688, 3072 |
| C922 | 192 … 3060 (11 alts) |
| Kiyo Pro (SuperSpeed) | 3072 and 33792 |
| 4c4a:4a55 | 3069 only |

  All four report bcdUVC 1.00. The VC-header clock is 30 MHz, except the C922 at 300 MHz. The claim that the C tool agrees has no evidence: the C tool prints these tables only after a successful open, which never happens on usbvideo.

Weakened:
- **Windows frame-number/QPC IOCTLs.** These work unelevated on both xHCI controllers and reproduce exactly: frame mod 2048 equals the hardware frame, past −10 works, −500 and future frames fail with error 87, and every hub fails with error 87. Median latency was 12–13 µs in the re-run and 18–20 µs originally. But:
  - The returned QPC is documented as a value predicted by the USB driver stack. The zero residual against 1250 ticks per microframe therefore only reflects the driver's linear model.
  - The documentation says PredictedAccuracy can be in 125 µs units, so "1" does not establish 1 µs.
  - In both runs, one sample returned a microframe-start QPC after the call had already returned (+7.2 µs and +2.2 µs), which contradicts ±1 µs accuracy.
  - Mapping each frame's SCR SOF to QPC is untested, because no stream exists yet.
- **pyuvc clock match.** The "2.7 µs" figure is not in the evidence file (0.15 µs there, 1.35 µs in the re-run, a single sample each). It shows the clocks share a domain, not a precision.

Confirmed from source or docs, untested on hardware:
- **pyuvc QPC-frequency bug.** get_precise_timestamp_freq never writes its output. The disassembly shows get_host_time_us works only because QPF writes into the same stack slot it divides by.
- **pyuvc bandwidth_factor.** It uses the Linux FIX_BANDWIDTH formula with the factor in place of bpp: 904 B per microframe for factor 2 and 681 (not 682) for factor 1.5.
- **WinUSB target.** Inbox winusb.inf's WINUSB model writes no DeviceInterfaceGUIDs, so the composite parent is the right target. The inherit-route dry run lists 'WinUsb Device'. The install, rollback and phase-2 scripts parse cleanly but have never been run.
- **libusb WinUSB isochronous rule.** Each transfer length must be a multiple of MaximumBytesPerInterval×8/interval.
- **macOS.** libusb's detach returns ACCESS without root or the com.apple.vm.device-access entitlement, and libuvc then refuses to claim. libusb issue #1014 is closed as a known limitation.
- **Linux.** USBDEVFS_DISCONNECT has no capability check, so a udev rule giving rw on the usbfs node is enough. FIX_BANDWIDTH (quirks=128) does not apply to MJPEG, because MJPEG formats carry UVC_FMT_FLAG_COMPRESSED. This needs reconciling with the user's experience.

Unverifiable: the libwdi/Zadig certificate details. The rollback script is the only artifact.

The overall verdict stands: libuvc is the most portable path. It needs a driver swap on Windows, a one-time udev rule on Linux, and root on macOS. Streaming, bandwidth-reduction effects and timing accuracy all remain unproven until phase 2.

result.topic: Adversarial verification of 'prior_art' (survey of cross-platform UVC capture libraries for MJPEG, timing, bandwidth, naming, portability)

verdicts.claim: GStreamer 1.28 mfvideosrc delivers camera-native MJPEG (image/jpeg caps, SOI/EOI, Pillow decode) for Kiyo Pro, C922, C930e at 1280x720@30
verdicts.reason: Original result.json numbers match (172/172, 155/155, 168/168; fps 29.95/30.27/30.08). Checked the bytes are camera-native: the Logitech samples have the Logitech marker layout (DQT first, zero-filled COM/APP0 placeholders, DRI, 4:2:2). The Kiyo sample has a different layout (JFIF+APP15, 4:2:0). That rules out a shared re-encoder. Source gstmfsourcereader.cpp@0701255 confirmed. Caveats: Pillow decoded only every 15th frame (12 of 172), and exposure was auto.
verdicts.rerun_numbers: Rerun 2026-10-25T18:50:50Z (results/windows/Gerald/verify_prior_art/gst_capture-mfvideosrc/): C922 172/172 valid (29.97 fps), Kiyo 155/155 (29.98), C930e 167/167 (29.99), plus USB Camera 4C4A 151/151 (25.76). A later rerun at 19:06:55Z (verify_prior_art/gst_capture-mfvideosrc-timeBeginPeriod1) had the Kiyo failing with 'Internal data stream error'. The Kiyo is intermittently faulty, see the Kiyo verdicts.

verdicts.claim: mfvideosrc PTS = running time when the sample reached the IMFSourceReader thread (host arrival); ksvideosrc PTS = arrival minus one frame duration
verdicts.reason: Source checked. gstmfsourcereader.cpp:485 sets clock_time = gst_mf_source_object_get_running_time() right after the synchronous ReadSample, and :635 uses it as the PTS. gstksvideosrc.c:853-855 has timestamp = clock_now - base_time - duration. The ks 33.3 ms offset holds by construction. The probe's clock mapping (perf_counter at pull minus (pipeline clock now - (base+pts))) uses one clock domain, so the comparison is valid.
verdicts.rerun_numbers: mf rerun arrival-PTS medians 0.120-0.131 ms (all 4 cameras). ks rerun 19:01:19Z: 33.40-33.43 ms medians on C922/C930e/USB Camera. Kiyo failed (not-negotiated).

verdicts.claim: Every arrival-type timestamp is quantized to ~16 ms steps (32/48 ms at 30 fps) on MF and KS paths, so the cause sits below MF; host/MF times alone cannot beat ~±8 ms
verdicts.reason: The quantization is real and reproducible. The 'cannot beat ±8 ms' part is an untested inference. Exact bin counts are off slightly: C930e mf 32x154/48x13 recomputed vs 149/13 claimed; Kiyo 118/21/9 vs 116/21/9. No committed script produces the histogram. New evidence: (a) the grid period is exactly 16.000 ms. Arrival phase mod 16 ms stays in one 1-ms bin for 94-100% of frames over 6 s, which a 15.625 ms timer tick would not do. (b) The phase differs between streams and runs, so the grid is set per stream rather than system-wide. (c) The system timer resolution was already 1.0 ms (NtQueryTimerResolution current=10000 x100ns), and timeBeginPeriod(1) in the capturing process left the ks and mf quantization unchanged. So the timer tick is ruled out, which supports a USB/usbvideo transfer-granularity cause (still unproven). The '±8 ms' bound is per raw timestamp only. Fitting a stable frame clock to the 32/48 dither pattern might recover phase better, and that was not tested.
verdicts.rerun_numbers: mf rerun: C930e 32x152/48x14, C922 32x157/48x14, Kiyo 32x139/48x13, 4C4A 32x86/48x64. ks rerun: C922 32x147/48x15 (plus 28x4, 36x5), C930e 32x146/48x13. With timeBeginPeriod(1) (verify_prior_art/gst_capture-{ks,mf}videosrc-timeBeginPeriod1, timer_res_*.json): ks C922 32x157/48x14, mf C930e 32x150/48x14, unchanged. Timer before/after = 1.0 ms. SDL3 rerun ts interval min/med/max 31.9/32.0/48.0 ms on C922/C930e/4C4A.

verdicts.claim: PyAV dshow vcodec=mjpeg passes MJPEG through for C922/C930e and opens by device path; Kiyo delivered rawvideo YUY2 at 720p and 1080p despite list_options showing MJPEG
verdicts.reason: C922/C930e passthrough and opening by path are confirmed. The Kiyo part is not reproducible and is confounded. (1) No 1080p result file exists; only prior_art_pyav_dshow-kiyo-720p and the default 720p runs. (2) The Kiyo rawvideo runs (18:13Z) fall in a window when the Kiyo was not in a normal state. Timing phase timing/registry_enable_metadata.log shows MetadataBufferSizeInKB0 written at 18:09:33Z with devnodes pending restart. mjpeg_mf_recheck/summary.json records MF_E_REBOOT_REQUIRED and a user replug at ~18:17Z. (3) On rerun, both 720p and 1080p failed to open with 'Could not RenderStream to connect pins' instead of giving rawvideo. The Kiyo also failed in KS/MF/SDL3 at 19:01-19:07Z, a transient fault the mjpeg phase also saw at 18:41-18:47Z. What can be said: FFmpeg dshow did not get MJPEG from the Kiyo in any run. The cause is unknown and not shown to be FFmpeg's.
verdicts.rerun_numbers: verify_prior_art/pyav_dshow-verify (19:04:01Z): C922 mjpeg 182/182, C930e mjpeg 182/182, USB Camera 4C4A mjpeg 156/156, Kiyo open failed (RenderStream). verify_prior_art/pyav_dshow-verify-kiyo-1080p (19:04:57Z): open failed (RenderStream). Open times 373-763 ms.

verdicts.claim: DirectShow device sample times are regularized (constant to 100 ns), carry no per-frame measurement, drift on C930e (-4.5 ms/s); wallclock mode graph-clock pts sits a constant ~30 ms before arrival
verdicts.reason: The regularization is confirmed and strengthened. In the rerun, USB Camera 4C4A pts deltas were a constant 333383 (nominal 30 fps) while it actually ran at about 25.8 fps, so arrival-pts drifted +143 ms/s. The device times are clearly synthesized from the nominal rate, not measured. The C930e numbers do not reproduce. Recomputed from the original file with frames[5:], the drift is -5.09 ms/s (claimed -4.5; no fit script exists). In the rerun all C930e deltas were 333333, with no second 333283 value, and drift was -1.79 ms/s. So 'drift -4.5 ms/s on the C930e' is one run's value, not a property. Wallclock mode: 1 ms resolution and a constant offset (spread 2.0-3.2 ms) are confirmed. But the ~30 ms is the difference between the DirectShow reference clock and the QueryPerformanceCounter clock behind perf_counter. Their epochs were not shown to match, so it should not be read as a latency. The original wallclock C930e run also ended with an unreported demux I/O error after 135 packets. The FFmpeg dshow_pin.c:321 comment ('PTS from video devices is unreliable') was confirmed.
verdicts.rerun_numbers: verify_prior_art/pyav_dshow-verify: distinct pts deltas C922 {333333}, C930e {333333}, 4C4A {333383}. Linear drift of arrival-pts: C922 +0.009 ms/s, C930e -1.79 ms/s, 4C4A +143 ms/s. Residual sd about 4-4.6 ms. Original files recomputed: C930e -5.09, Kiyo -0.95, C922 -0.012 ms/s.

verdicts.claim: SDL3 3.4.18 MF backend delivers raw MJPEG (pitch = byte length) for all 4 cameras incl. Kiyo; name only; timestamp = IMFSample time rebased to SDL_GetTicksNS
verdicts.reason: Source confirmed: SDL_camera_mediafoundation.c:453-458 uses IMFSample_GetSampleTime x100, and :478-479 sets pitch = buflen for MJPG. SDL_camera.c:862-866 rebases at the first frame. The original numbers are in result.json. The rerun confirms C922, C930e and 4C4A. For the Kiyo (faulty at the time), SDL handed back 179 surfaces labelled SDL_PIXELFORMAT_MJPG whose 'pitch' was 1280 bytes. None were JPEG, and their timestamps had un-quantized 33.3 ms intervals. So an MJPG-labelled surface is not guaranteed to hold JPEG bytes, and pitch-as-length is not guaranteed either. Applications must validate.
verdicts.rerun_numbers: verify_prior_art/sdl3_camera (19:05:19Z): C922 170/170, USB Camera 152/152 (26.1 fps), C930e 167/167, Kiyo 0/179 valid (every payload 1280 bytes, surface_format MJPG). opened_camera_properties [] for all.

verdicts.claim: pygrabber 0.2: forced RGB24, SampleTime dropped, names only; lists only FORMAT_VideoInfo so the Kiyo shows a single YUY2 format
verdicts.reason: The RGB24, dropped-SampleTime and FriendlyName parts are confirmed in source: dshow_graph.py@f0090e0 line 387 sets RGB24, and BufferCB at line 611 ignores SampleTime. The causal claim about the Kiyo is refuted. openpnp-capture uses the same FORMAT_VideoInfo-only filter (platformcontext.cpp:362), and 81 s later (18:16:18Z) it listed 16 Kiyo formats including MJPG. My pygrabber rerun lists 16 Kiyo formats [H264, MJPG, NV12, YUY2]. The single-YUY2 listing at 18:14:57Z came from the Kiyo's abnormal state in that window (registry change at 18:09, replug at ~18:17), not from the format filter.
verdicts.rerun_numbers: verify_prior_art/pygrabber (19:08:50Z): C922 36 formats, USB Camera 9, Kiyo 16 [H264, MJPG, NV12, YUY2] (no callback: Kiyo stream fault), C930e 34. Callbacks were [720,1280,3] uint8.

verdicts.claim: openpnp-capture 0.0.30: name + DevicePath ID, RGB only (w*h*3 buffer), no timestamp API
verdicts.reason: result.json: buffer 2764800 = 1280*720*3; first bytes are not FFD8; frame-counter rates 29.9/25.7/30.1/30.2. Source: platformcontext.cpp:151-162 (uniqueID = name + ' ' + DevicePath), platformstream.cpp:393 (MEDIASUBTYPE_RGB24). Not rerun (enumeration/RGB result, low risk). Note: the Kiyo was opened at a nominal 60 fps format.

verdicts.reason: All values are present in prior_art_gst_list/result.json. Not rerun. No stability across reconnect was tested and none is claimed. Note that the MI_00 instance segment (e.g. 8&268da596) is a parent-derived ID whose stability across ports or reboots is unverified.

verdicts.claim: Linux uvcvideo FIX_BANDWIDTH guarded by !(format->flags & UVC_FMT_FLAG_COMPRESSED) in v3.2/v4.4/v5.15/v6.1/master; quirks read at probe
verdicts.reason: Fetched the source. Master@21a7f44 uvc_video.c:229-231. v3.2 (drivers/media/video/uvc) :122, v4.4 :130, v5.15 :195, v6.1 :201. uvc_driver.c:2214 is in probe, and module_param quirks/hwtimestamps are 0644. verdicts.claim: Linux buffer timestamp = CLOCK_MONOTONIC at first payload (SOE); clock recovery only if hwtimestamps != 0; metadata node
verdicts.reason: Source checked. uvc_queue.c:250-251 sets TIMESTAMP_MONOTONIC|TSTAMP_SRC_SOE. uvc_video.c:1270 sets the timestamp on FID flip via uvc_video_get_time() (ktime_get unless clock=realtime, :504-509). :829 has 'if (!uvc_hw_timestamps_param) return;'. Documented-untested; the metadata doc page was not re-opened.

verdicts.claim: Pupil libuvc fork maps PTS to host clock (QPC/CLOCK_MONOTONIC/mach) via SCR + iso timing; bandwidth_factor default 2.0; formula; '1.5 needed for 3 HS cameras'
verdicts.reason: Source checked. pupil-labs/libuvc@949cb47 stream.c:558-571 (QPC/CLOCK_MONOTONIC/mach_absolute_time), :577-600 (frame_ts = dev_clk_start_host_us + dev_time(PTS)), :1417 copies it to capture_time, and pyuvc uvc_bindings.pyx:755 maps capture_time to frame.timestamp. :1156-1162 holds the formula and the quoted comment. Minor correction: the rate term is (10000000/dwFrameInterval + 1), i.e. fps+1, not fps. Wheels and upload time 2026-10-21 were confirmed on PyPI. README confirms libusbK on Windows and that non-root is not possible on macOS. Accuracy is untested.

verdicts.claim: Upstream libuvc v0.0.8 parses PTS/SCR but doesn't export them; only capture_time_finished set; altsetting from dwMaxPayloadTransferSize
verdicts.reason: v0.0.8 stream.c:689 (CLOCK_MONOTONIC into capture_time_finished), :696-697 (hold_last_scr/hold_pts), :1173 (dwMaxPayloadTransferSize), :1400 (only capture_time_finished copied). libuvc.h:477 declares capture_time, which is never set. Release published 2026-09-13T04:48:49Z (gh api).

verdicts.claim: macOS 12+ libusb/libuvc needs root; com.apple.vm.device-access not granted to non-VM apps (libusb #1014)
verdicts.reason: gh api: #1014 closed 2025-05-21 (state_reason completed). The 'no real solution, this is a macOS limitation' wording is the issue title, not a closing statement. Comment 2021-10-30 quotes Apple DTS saying the entitlement is for VM apps. pyuvc README: non-root 'currently not possible'. Documented-untested.

verdicts.claim: Windows usbvideo.sys exposes UVC PTS/SCR via MetadataId_UsbVideoHeader when MetadataBufferSizeInKB<Pin> is set; librealsense does this
verdicts.reason: The Microsoft page and librealsense are confirmed. realsense_metadata_win10.ps1 writes MetadataBufferSizeInKB0-3 under DeviceClasses...\#global\Device Parameters. mf-uvc.cpp:91-108 reads MFSampleExtension_CaptureMetadata, then MF_CAPTURE_METADATA_FRAME_RAWSTREAM, then MetadataId_UsbVideoHeader. But the same Microsoft page also says 'a custom INF is required for the given hardware for metadata to come through' and frames the registry value as custom-metadata support. Whether a bare registry write works for generic webcams is unproven. The timing phase's registry write (timing/registry_enable_metadata.log) left devnodes needing a restart, and the Kiyo was abnormal afterwards.

verdicts.claim: No macOS MJPEG passthrough in surveyed libraries; videoSettings={} = device-native format
verdicts.reason: Grep found no jpeg/MJPG/dmb1 strings in avfvideosrc.m@0701255 or in SDL_camera_coremedia.m release-3.4.18. FFmpeg avfoundation and the Apple doc page were not re-opened by me. Documented-untested; only the draft can answer this.

verdicts.reason: UVCCamera stream.c:1222-1237 (uvc_start_streaming_bandwidth, factor [0,1]). nusb #47 state open (gh api). libusb v1.0.30 ChangeLog: 'Windows: Add support for isochronous transfers with WinUSB' in the section above v1.0.22, i.e. v1.0.23.
